181	/** One medicine on the patient's self-reported My Medicines list. */
182	export interface MyMed {
183	  type: 'my_med';
184	
185	  /** HomeLog's id for this medicine on the list. Stable across saves of the list. */
186	  homelog_med_id: string;
187	
188	  /** The name as the patient entered it: brand, generic or nickname ("water pill"). Not normalized. */
189	  name: string;
190	
191	  /**
192	   * Set when the patient picked the name from HomeLog's drug search instead of typing it. `rxnorm` is
193	   * the RxNorm concept the search result was linked to (ingredient + strength + form when the patient
194	   * picked a specific product, otherwise just an ingredient). Absent for typed names.
195	   */
196	  picked_from_search?: { rxnorm: string; display: string };
197	
198	  /** Strength as the patient wrote it, free text (e.g. "500 mg", "100 units/mL pen"). Absent if left blank. */
199	  strength_text?: string;
200	
201	  /** How the patient says they take it, free text, in their words. May disagree with the prescription. */
202	  how_i_take_it?: string;
203	
204	  /**
205	   * Whether the patient is taking it now, by their account.
206	   * - 'taking': currently taking (including "as needed" medicines they still use).
207	   * - 'stopped': no longer taking. The patient keeps stopped medicines on the list as history.
208	   * HomeLog has no "paused" status; patients usually mark a paused medicine 'stopped' and explain in
209	   * `note`, or leave it 'taking'.
210	   */
211	  status: 'taking' | 'stopped';
212	
213	  /** When the patient started it, from a month picker: `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM` or `YYYY-MM-DD`; precision is the string's precision. Absent if not entered. */
214	  started?: string;
215	
216	  /** When the patient stopped it, same format as `started`. Present only when `status` is 'stopped', and not always then. */
217	  stopped?: string;
218	
219	  /**
220	   * - 'prescription': the patient says a clinician prescribed it.
221	   * - 'over_the_counter': bought without a prescription (includes supplements).
222	   */
223	  kind: 'prescription' | 'over_the_counter';
224	
225	  /** Patient's free-text note (why stopped, who prescribed, side effects). */
226	  note?: string;
227	}

140	  status: 'active' | 'held' | 'stopped' | 'unknown';
141	  /**
142	   * Local date on which the current status began according to this source: for 'held' or 'stopped',
143	   * the date of the hold or stop; for 'active', the date the source's current line or order started
144	   * (or resumed). Keep the source's precision. Omit if the source does not say.
145	   */
146	  status_since?: PartialDate;
147	  /**
148	   * Amount per administration currently prescribed (for 'held' and 'stopped': the amount when it was
149	   * held or stopped). For a patient's own list: the amount the patient says they take, if they give
150	   * one; a direction that names no count ("morning", "bedtime") means one tablet or capsule. `unit` is
151	   * one of the listed units; convert source spellings ("unit", "UNT", "[iU]" -> "units"). Express an
152	   * amount in tablets as a mass when the record gives the strength per tablet ("200 mg" strength,
153	   * "take 2" -> 400 mg); use 'tablet' only when the strength is unknown. Omit when the source gives no
154	   * single amount (a range such as "1 or 2", a sliding scale).
155	   */
156	  dose?: { value: number; unit: 'mg' | 'mcg' | 'units' | 'mL' | 'tablet' };
157	  /**
158	   * How often, normalized: 'QD' once daily, 'BID' twice daily, 'TID' three times daily, 'QHS' once
159	   * daily at bedtime, 'QW' once weekly, 'PRN' as needed, 'other' anything else. Omit if unknown.

content.text:
I revised the mapper and saved the new version to `out/transform.ts`. It type-checks and runs cleanly on the sample patients through `check.sh`. The samples include the same levothyroxine case as the feedback, and it now comes out as 75 mg. I haven't been able to re-run it on the other patients behind the feedback.

**The fix:** the one wrong row was a levothyroxine dose. The patient picked "levothyroxine sodium 0.075 MG Oral Tablet" from the drug search, so 75 mcg, but typed the strength as "75 mg". My earlier mapper treated that as a mg/mcg typing slip and output 75 mcg from the search result. The expected output is 75 mg.

**Judgment call:** the views define a patient-list dose as "the amount the patient says they take". So the patient's own strength text now always wins, and the drug-search product name is only a fallback when that text is blank or can't be read. This also changes a second case: before, when the two disagreed by more than a mg/mcg slip, the mapper left the dose out. Now it uses the patient's figure there too, because the same rule applies. A clinically implausible number like this one is still passed through as written, not corrected, since that is what the expected output asks for.

Everything else is the same as the previous version.
